desc: Split the pattern `p` into three components: `pre` (before first `*`), `mid` (between `*`s), and `suf` (after second `*`), and store their lengths.
Implement the KMP `compute_pi` and `search` helper functions to efficiently find occurrences of `pre`, `mid`, and `suf` in `s`.
Handle the special case where `mid` is empty (pattern is `pre + * + suf`).
Implement the general case where `mid` is not empty:
Precompute `best_pre[i]`: the start index of the latest `pre` occurrence ending $\le i$.
Precompute `best_suf[i]`: the end index of the earliest `suf` occurrence starting $\ge i$.
Iterate through each occurrence of `mid` at `[m_start, m_end]`, use `best_pre[m_start]` and `best_suf[m_end + 1]` to calculate the shortest valid substring length.
Combine all logic into the `shortestMatchingSubstring` method.
Verify the solution against provided examples.
Ensure the class structure matches the starter code exactly.
Check for any potential off-by-one errors in index calculations.
